title: Hardware profiles workload matrix (draft) — seq buckets, concurrency, pass/fail
content:
Context / why this exists
- We need a workload matrix that is representative enough to validate hardware tuning profiles (H100 / L40S / B200) without exploding runtime or adding too many degrees of freedom.
- This is intentionally a draft. Goal is to converge on: (1) a minimal matrix used as perf gates in CI/perf-canary, and (2) a larger nightly matrix for deeper coverage.

Primary consumers
- Runtime Scheduling (Sofia/Lena/Marcus): needs concurrency + queue/backpressure stress.
- Kernels (Hiro/Yuki/Grace/Isabella): needs seq-length buckets for kernel autoselection and prefill/decode behavior.
- KV-cache/memory (Omar/Samir): needs long-context + high-concurrency to find fragmentation/OOM.
- SRE/perf-canary (Aisha/Kira V): needs crisp pass/fail thresholds (low noise, actionable regressions).

Non-goals (for this matrix)
- Model quality / alignment scoring (handled separately; this matrix is serving perf/stability).
- Customer-specific workloads (we will keep a slot for ‘customer replay’ later but not gate on it).
- Exotic kernels / brand-new features still behind heavy flags.

Definitions
- Prefill tokens: input/prompt length.
- Decode tokens: output length generated.
- Concurrency: number of in-flight requests per replica (or per scheduler instance).
- Streaming: server sends chunks incrementally; we care about cadence / time-to-first-token (TTFT) and tail stalls.
- Errors include: non-2xx, retries, timeouts, OOM kills, scheduler queue overflow/429.

Dimension 0: Hardware SKUs / deployment variants (baseline coverage)
- H100 (SXM + PCIe variants exist; assume we normalize clocks via guardrails where possible)
- L40S (memory constrained relative to H100; higher risk of OOM on long context)
- B200 (experimental / gated; limited fleet access; matrix must have a ‘minimal bring-up slice’)

Dimension 1: Model families (proposed)
We should pick a small set that stresses different kernel paths and KV-cache behavior. Candidate families:
A) Llama-family dense decoder-only (baseline)
B) Mixtral-style MoE decoder-only (routing overhead, memory layout differences)
C) “Small + fast” model (sensitive to CPU/runtime overhead and scheduling)
D) Long-context tuned variant (if we have one in catalog; otherwise emulate with long prompts)

Proposed concrete model slots (names intentionally generic here — we’ll map to catalog IDs per environment)
- M1: Dense 8B-ish chat
- M2: Dense 70B-ish chat (or equivalent large dense)
- M3: MoE ~8x7B-ish
- M4: Small 3B–7B-ish

Notes
- For L40S gating, M2 may be too heavy unless quantized or restricted; we can do M2 only on H100/B200 and run M1/M3/M4 on L40S.
- For B200 bring-up, start with M1 and M4 only.

Dimension 2: Request archetypes (proposed)
We need archetypes that isolate prefill vs decode, and stress streaming and tool-calling-ish patterns.

Archetype list (v0)
1) Chat short: short prompt, moderate decode
2) Chat medium: medium prompt, moderate decode
3) Summarization: long prefill, short decode
4) Long-context chat: very long prefill, moderate decode (KV-cache pressure)
5) Code-ish: medium prefill, longer decode (decode-heavy)
6) Tool-calling pattern (approx): prompt includes function schema + prior tool outputs; moderate prefill; short decode but sensitive to TTFT and jitter

Open question: do we need “stop-and-go” streaming (client pauses / backpressure) now? Probably later.

Dimension 3: Sequence length buckets
We should define buckets as (prefill tokens, decode tokens). Values below are initial; adjust after first week of runs to match typical traffic distributions.

Bucket set (target)
- S (short): prefill 256, decode 128
- M (medium): prefill 1,024, decode 256
- L (long prefill): prefill 4,096, decode 128
- XL (very long prefill): prefill 16,384, decode 256 (run only on SKUs/profiles that claim support; L40S likely excluded or run with strict guardrails)
- D (decode-heavy): prefill 512, decode 1,024

Additional notes
- Streaming runs should use same token budgets; we measure TTFT and inter-token/chunk cadence.
- We should pin sampling params to reduce variance: temperature low-ish (0–0.2) for determinism, top_p 1.0, fixed seed where possible.

Dimension 4: Concurrency / load levels
We should cover:
- Low concurrency to catch pure kernel regressions
- “Normal” concurrency to match typical continuous batching usage
- High concurrency to stress queueing/backpressure and reveal tail latency

Concurrency levels (per replica) — draft
- C1: 1 (single in-flight)
- C4: 4
- C16: 16
- C32: 32 (may be too high for large models; allow per-model cap)

Potential rule-of-thumb caps
- M4 (small): can run up to C32
- M1 (8B): up to C16/C32 depending on SKU
- M3 (MoE): up to C16 (watch memory)
- M2 (large): up to C4/C8 only

Dimension 5: Streaming vs non-streaming
We should run both for at least one bucket per archetype because streaming regressions have shown up even when aggregate TPS improves.

Minimal streaming coverage proposal
- For each (SKU, profile, model) run:
  - Non-streaming: S, M, L, D
  - Streaming: S and M (plus L on H100/B200)

Metrics captured (must-have)
Latency
- TTFT (streaming)
- Time-to-last-token (end-to-end)
- p50 / p95 / p99 for TTFT and end-to-end
Throughput
- Output tokens/sec (aggregate)
- Requests/sec
- Prefill tokens/sec (if available) and decode tokens/sec split
Stability
- Error rate (5xx/timeout/retry)
- OOM count / GPU reset / process restarts
- Queue drops / rate-limit responses (429) when backpressure triggers
Resource
- Peak GPU memory (and/or steady-state)
- KV-cache utilization / eviction counters
- CPU utilization (to catch “small model gets slower” due to overhead)

Pass/fail criteria (draft)
We need two categories: (A) hard safety gates and (B) perf regression thresholds.

A) Hard safety gates (always fail)
- Any OOM kill or GPU reset in the gating slice.
- Error rate > 0.1% (excluding intentional 429s if the test is explicitly a backpressure test; by default, treat 429 as fail).
- Streaming TTFT p95 regression > 20% vs baseline for the same (model, bucket, concurrency) when profile enabled.
- Any sustained streaming stall: >2s without a chunk for >0.5% of requests (needs a precise definition in the runner; placeholder for now).

B) Performance regression thresholds (draft; tune after we see noise)
We compare candidate profile vs baseline profile/runtime on same SKU.
- End-to-end latency p95: must be within +10% for ‘balanced’ profiles on S and M buckets.
- Throughput (output tokens/sec): should improve by at least +5% on at least 2 of the 4 non-streaming buckets (S/M/L/D) for the tuned profile to be considered “worth shipping”.
- Tail sensitivity clause: if throughput improves but p99 latency regresses > +15% on any bucket at C16 (or max concurrency for that model), mark as “investigate” and block promotion from canary -> wider rollout.

Special handling for throughput-first modes
- If profile is explicitly labeled throughput-first, allow p95 end-to-end up to +20% regression, but require throughput +10% on M and D buckets.

Special handling for B200 experimental
- Bring-up pass criteria is stability-first: no OOMs, error rate <= 0.1%, and throughput not worse than H100 baseline by more than 15% for M1/M4 on S/M buckets (this is a placeholder; may be unrealistic depending on availability/stack maturity).

Proposed matrix: “gating slice” (CI/perf-canary)
Goal: keep runtime under ~60–90 minutes per SKU runner (tbd; depends on runner availability).

Gating slice v0
- Models: M1 (dense 8B-ish), M4 (small)
- Buckets: S, M, D
- Concurrency: C1, C16 (for M4: also C32 if stable)
- Streaming: S (C16)
- Runs per point: 3 (median of medians) to reduce noise; consider 5 if p95 is too noisy.

This yields per SKU roughly:
- M1: (S,M,D) x (C1,C16) + streaming(S,C16) = 7 points
- M4: same plus optional (C32) = 7–10 points
Total: ~14–17 points per SKU per profile build.

Proposed matrix: “nightly expanded”
- Add M3 (MoE) with S/M/L at C4/C16 (streaming S)
- Add L bucket for M1 on H100/B200
- Add XL bucket on H100 only (and only for profiles that claim long-context support)
- Add archetype-specific prompt templates (summarization + tool-calling)

Text table (rough) — Expanded
SKU: H100
- M1: S/M/L/D/XL @ C1/C4/C16, stream S/M/L
- M2: S/M/L @ C1/C4, non-stream + stream S
- M3: S/M/L @ C1/C4/C16, stream S
- M4: S/M/D @ C1/C16/C32, stream S

SKU: L40S
- M1: S/M/L/D @ C1/C4/C16 (cap if OOM risk), stream S/M
- M3: S/M @ C1/C4/C16, stream S
- M4: S/M/D @ C1/C16/C32, stream S
(no M2 by default; if we do, it must be quantized + explicit KV-cache budget)

SKU: B200 (experimental)
- Bring-up: M4 + M1 only, S/M/D @ C1/C4/C16, stream S
- Expand once stable: add M3 S/M

Prompt distributions / realism (notes from Applied ML)
- Current perf suite prompts are too uniform; we should mix:
  - 60% short chat (S)
  - 25% medium (M)
  - 10% long prefill (L)
  - 5% decode-heavy (D)
- Tool-calling approximation: include function schema + 1–2 tool outputs; keep deterministic generation.
- Include a small % of “pathological” prompts (e.g., near-bucket-boundary lengths) in nightly runs only.

Operational notes / what we should log in artifacts
- Effective profile name + version + override source (fleet default vs env var vs config file)
- Scheduler knobs snapshot (queue limits, batching caps, fairness toggles)
- KV-cache budget values and any eviction/pressure counters
- GPU SKU detection string + normalized SKU
- CUDA/driver version (especially for B200)

Open questions / TODOs
1) Tokenization: do we pre-generate tokenized inputs to reduce variance across tokenizer versions, or do we pin tokenizer version in runner? (lean pin tokenizer + store token counts)
2) Duration per run: fixed #requests vs fixed time window? (I lean fixed #requests for comparability; but time-window is better for steady-state throughput)
3) What do we treat as baseline? runtime hard-coded defaults or “previous profile pack version”?
4) Streaming cadence metric: need a clear, implementable definition in benchmark-lab runner.
5) L40S guardrails: define strict KV-cache budgets for L/XL; decide if XL is always excluded.
6) Backpressure tests: do we include a dedicated overload test that expects 429 and verifies graceful degradation? Probably nightly only; not in gating.

Proposed next steps
- (Claire/Rina) Convert gating slice into runner config for benchmark-lab PR-1842 follow-ups.
- (Aisha/Kira V) Propose initial perf-canary thresholds using the pass/fail draft above; run 1 week and tighten.
- (Sofia/Lena/Omar) Review concurrency caps and L40S memory guardrails assumptions.
- (Hiro/Yuki) Verify seq buckets align with kernel autoselect buckets (H100 heuristic work).

Changelog
- 2025-11-28: initial draft created (Claire)
- 2025-12-03: added tool-calling archetype and streaming TTFT gating note after Applied ML feedback
- 2025-12-10: added explicit gating slice vs nightly split; added L40S model exclusions and B200 bring-up slice
